title: Tri-screen portable monitors aren’t for the faint of heart
gist: Hands-on review of KYY's X90G ($360), a tri-screen portable monitor with three 15.6-inch 1080p IPS panels around a laptop. The author finds it useful for multi-document research but bulky (6.4 lb, ~46 inches wide unfolded), bezel-heavy and never unified, concluding it is overkill for most portable-monitor buyers.

insights.claim: KYY's X90G tri-screen portable monitor costs about $360 and has three 15.6-inch 1920x1080 IPS screens rated up to 400 nits, each with independent tilt and controls.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding

insights.claim: KYY's X90G differentiates from rival tri-screen monitors by placing screens left, right and above the laptop and by supporting Linux and Android in addition to Windows and macOS, but it does not fit laptops larger than 17.3 inches.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding

insights.claim: Tri-screen portable monitors involve a hard trade-off between portability and screen space: the KYY X90G weighs 6.4 pounds, more than twice an ultralight Dell XPS, and spans about 46 inches with side panels flat.

insights.claim: Unlike some dual-screen portable monitors, a triple portable monitor cannot function as a single unified display, and its bezels and misaligned screens make it feel like four separate displays.

insights.so_what: Dual-screen designs may be the better-selling form factor versus tri-screen.
